hints.title: Keep the target fixed while testing each direction
hints.body: The target says that ab is divisible by n. Sufficiency asks whether divisibility of either factor guarantees the target. Necessity asks whether the target forces divisibility of either factor.
hints.recap: Necessary and sufficient are two different implications.
hints.pitfall: Do not swap the target with the proposed condition midway through a test.
hints.pause: Write the direction you need to prove for sufficiency.

recall.reminder: Necessary and sufficient are two different implications.

hints.title: Write a multiple algebraically
hints.body: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> divides <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math>, write <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> with integer <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> and substitute into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow></math>. Repeat the argument if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> divides <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: Divisibility means equality to an integer multiple.
hints.pitfall: The word or allows either factor to supply the multiple.
hints.pause: Decide what this proves about one direction of the implication.

recall.reminder: Divisibility means equality to an integer multiple.

hints.title: Test the reverse direction
hints.body: Try a composite <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> whose proper factors can be split between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></math>. Check divisibility of the product and of the individual factors separately.
hints.recap: A product can acquire divisibility from both factors together.
hints.pitfall: Choose positive integers, as required in the question.
hints.pause: Construct a valid example, then classify both implication directions.

recall.reminder: A product can acquire divisibility from both factors together.

solution:
1. Prove sufficiency. If a=nk, then ab=n(kb) is divisible by n. If it is b that is divisible by n, the same argument works with the factors exchanged.

2. Test necessity. Take a=b=2 and n=4. Then ab=4 is divisible by n, but neither 2 is divisible by 4. The target can hold without the proposed condition.

The condition is sufficient but not necessary: B.
knowledgePattern: Separate divisibility sufficiency from the false composite-divisor converse
